messages:
emma: morning all, posted a pic of my balcony-office 14 tiny folding standing desk, string lights, and a fishbowl planter. love it except for the construction next door. since 9am there's jackhammering and my call audio clicks + wifi spikes/drops. anyone had construction-era wifi/noise hacks? (pic: https://i.imgur.com/balcony-office.jpg) :construction_worker:
jon: ugh. I had that last year. first try: power-cycle router and move it off the floor, elevation matters for antennas. also try 5GHz vs 2.4GHz (5GHz less congested but shorter range).
rachel: seconding jon. also try changing channel  many routers auto pick a DFS channel that gets intermittent radar pauses near construction equipment. on linux you can scan with `sudo iwlist wlan0 scan` or use wifi analyzer on your phone.
emma: any quick home fixes tonight? i can't run ethernet to the balcony.
jon: if running cable impossible, try a USB-C gigabit adapter and place a small travel router by the sliding door, then create a little LAN bridge. OR try a powerline adapter kit (TP-Link AV1000) if your building wiring is decent.
rachel: for audio clicks, use a wired headset if possible. for pings, run `ping 8.8.8.8` during hammering and paste results. if you see packet loss spikes at the exact times of bangs, it's prob radio interference or router overload.
emma: ran ping during a 5-min window: packet loss jumps to 40% at 09:12 then fine. attached screenshot.
jon: yep that's correlated. also check your router logs  if it's reassociating clients you'll see auth/timeouts.
deploy-bot: NOTE: Reminder  please be mindful of scheduled maintenance windows; post any noisy work to #facilities so teammates can plan. (automated)
emma: thanks everyone. trying a temporary travel router + towel-sandwich around the balcony to dampen sound (lol). i'll post an update and a before/after ping screenshot. :coffee:
